task_instance: For a Fathom CRM-sync failure support case, produce the redacted Fathom debug bundle the skill describes: run its debug-collection script to probe Fathom API connectivity (HTTP status/auth state), fetch recent-meeting metadata and latest-transcript availability, capture rate-limit headers, and pack them into a debug-fathom-<timestamp>.tar.gz archive with a summary.txt.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is generated by running its bundled bash debug-collection script, which shells out to a curl HTTP client against the Fathom API and then packs the results with tar into a compressed archive. The office-assistant runtime grants only reading/writing/editing text files and web fetch/search; it cannot run any shell command or code and cannot produce a binary (tar.gz) file, so the script cannot be executed and the archive cannot be created. The actual evidence the bundle must contain (live API HTTP status, recent-meeting JSON, transcript-status JSON, rate-limit headers) can only come from executing that script. Compounding blockers: the script also requires a FATHOM_API_KEY credential and reaching the Fathom API host, and in this copy every Fathom endpoint URL is replaced by an unreachable placeholder; fabricating the data the script would return is disallowed. Only sample support-case input could be authored by hand; the collected-diagnostics deliverable itself cannot be produced or verified.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md at the skill path. Its core workflow (sections 'Debug Collection Script' and 'Analyzing the Bundle') is a #!/bin/bash script using curl against Fathom API endpoints with the X-Api-Key header, jq parsing, and 'tar -czf' to emit debug-fathom-<ts>.tar.gz. The stated Output is 'A minimal redacted diagnostic bundle with owner, scope, evidence, and safe escalation/recovery path', whose evidence is the script's collected API output. The runtime prohibits shell/code execution and binary-file creation, so neither the collection nor the archive can be produced; no file beyond result.json was written to the work directory. Secondary blockers would also apply (no FATHOM_API_KEY/account, and placeholder-only API endpoints that are unreachable).
